dnsMode.description:
In 'cname' dnsMode, Control Plane will configure workloads to accept traffic for the domain but will not manage DNS records for the domain.
      End users configure CNAME records in their own DNS pointed to the canonical workload endpoint.
      Currently 'cname' dnsMode requires that a tls.serverCertificate is configured when subdomain based routing is used.
      In 'ns' dnsMode, Control Plane will manage the subdomains and create all necessary DNS records.
      End users configure an NS record to forward DNS requests to the Control Plane managed DNS servers.

gvcLink.description: One of gvcLink and routes may be provided. When gvcLink is configured each workload in the GVC will receive a subdomain in the form ${workload.name}.${domain.name}

replacePrefix.description: When provided, the URI prefix will be replaced with this string before the request is sent to the workload.

regex.description:
Used to match URI paths.
One of prefix OR regex may be provided.
Uses the google re2 regex syntax

hostPrefix.description:
This option allows forwarding traffic for different host headers to different workloads.
This will only be used when the target GVC has dedicated load balancing enabled and the Domain is configure for wildcard support.
Contact your account manager for details.

hostRegex.description:
A regex to match the host header. 
This will only be used when the target GVC has dedicated load balancing enabled and the Domain is configure for wildcard support. 
Contact your account manager for details.

set.description: Sets or overrides headers to all http requests for this route.

headers.description: Modify the headers for all http requests for this route.

replica.description: The replica number of a stateful workload to route to. If not provided, traffic will be routed to all replicas.

workloadLink.description: The workload to mirror traffic to.

port.description: The port to send mirrored traffic to. If not provided, traffic will be mirrored to the first discovered port on the mirrored workload

percent.description: The percentage of traffic to mirror to the specified workload.

items.description: Mirror a percentage of traffic to another workload for testing or canary purposes.

workloadLink.description: The canary workload to route a weighted percentage of traffic to.

port.description: The port to send canary traffic to. If not provided, the first configured port on the workload is used.

weight.description: The percentage of traffic to send to this canary workload. A weight of 0 disables the canary so it can be toggled on and off without removing it.

items.description: Routes a weighted percentage of traffic to an additional workload. The combined weight of all canaries on a route must not exceed 100; the remaining weight goes to the primary workload. A canary with a weight of 0 is skipped. A canary whose workload is not deployed in a given location is dropped there and its weight returns to the primary workload. On tcp ports the weight applies per connection rather than per request.

canaries.description: Split traffic for this route across one or more additional workloads by weight.

routes.description: A list of mappings to workloads.

secretLink.description: The secret will include a client certificate authority cert in PEM format used to verify requests which include client certificates. The key subject must match the domain and the key usage properties must be configured for client certificate authorization. The secret type must be keypair.

clientCertificate.description: When clientCertificate is defined, requests may optionally supply a client certificate. The certificate details are included in the x-forwarded-client-cert header.

secretLink.description: When provided, this is used as the server certificate authority. The secret type must be keypair and the content must be PEM encoded.

serverCertificate.description: Configure an optional custom server certificate for the domain. When the port number is 443 and this is not supplied, a certificate is provisioned automatically.

tls.description: Used for TLS connections for this Domain. End users are responsible for certificate updates.

routingTier.description: Routing tier for DNS geo routing. Lower value = higher priority. Locations with the same routingTier form a group; within a group, lowest latency wins. If all locations in the highest-priority group are unavailable, the next group is used.

latencyOffsetMs.description: Artificial latency offset in milliseconds added to measured latency. Positive values push traffic away from this location, negative values attract traffic. Default: 0.

latencyToleranceMs.description: Maximum acceptable latency in milliseconds. If measured latency exceeds this latencyToleranceMs, the location is treated as unavailable for DNS geo routing.

locationOptions.description: Per-location routing options for DNS geo routing. Allows configuring priority-based failover and latency adjustments per location.

endpointNamingFormat.description:
Customizes the subdomain format for the canonical workload endpoint.
`default` leaves it as ${workloadName}-${gvcName}.cpln.app
`org` follows the scheme ${workloadName}-${gvcName}.${org}.cpln.app

aliasWorkloadLink.description:
Workload in this GVC whose canonical endpoint backs the GVC alias DNS record.
When set, ${alias}.cpln.app is published as a CNAME to the workload's canonical endpoint,
inheriting its HTTP health probes and per-location geo failover. When unset, the alias
resolves directly to cluster ingress endpoints with no application-level health awareness.
Has no effect while the referenced workload is globally suspended (defaultOptions.suspend
or defaultOptions.autoscaling.maxScale == 0); per-location suspends are ignored.

recoveryPolicy.description: Only applicable to persistent volumes, this determines what Control Plane will do when creating a new workload replica if a corresponding volume exists.

path.description: Mount path inside the container. Required for non-vm workloads; rejected for type=vm.

name.description: VM disk name. Required for type=vm; rejected for other workload types.

bus.description: VM disk bus. Only valid for type=vm. A cpln://secret/ volume on a sata or scsi bus is presented to the guest as a read-only CD-ROM.

bootOrder.description: VM disk boot order. Only valid for type=vm.

env.description: These environment variables will be available to any workload in the GVC. Note: a workload must opt-in to receive these variables.

dedicated.description: Creates a dedicated load balancer in each location and enables additional Domain features: custom ports, protocols and wildcard hostnames. Charges apply for each location.

trustedProxies.description:
Controls the address used for request logging and for setting the X-Envoy-External-Address header.
If set to 1, then the last address in an existing X-Forwarded-For header will be used in place of the source client IP address.
If set to 2, then the second to last address in an existing X-Forwarded-For header will be used in place of the source client IP address. If the XFF header does not have at least two addresses or does not exist then the source client IP address will be used instead.

status5xx.description: Specify the redirect url for any 500 level status code

status401.description:
An optional url redirect for 401 responses.
Supports envoy format strings to include request information.
E.g. https://your-oauth-server/oauth2/authorize?return_to=%REQ(:path)%&client_id=your-client-id

class.description: Specify the redirect url for all status codes in a class

redirect.description: Specify the url to be redirected to for different http status codes.

ipSet.description: A link to an IPSet resource that will be used for this load balancer

enabled.description:
Enable KEDA for this GVC.
KEDA is a Kubernetes-based event-driven autoscaler that allows you to scale workloads based on external events.
When enabled,a keda operator will be deployed in the GVC and workloads in the GVC can use KEDA to scale based on external metrics.

identityLink.description:
A link to an Identity resource that will be used for KEDA.
This will allow the keda operator to access cloud and network resources.

secrets.description:
A list of secrets to be used as TriggerAuthentication objects.
The TriggerAuthentication object will be named after the secret and can be used by triggers on workloads in this GVC.

max.description: Number of responses allowed on the replyTo subject, -1 means no limit

ttl.description: Deadline to send replies on the replyTo subject [#ms(millis) | #s(econds) | m(inutes) | h(ours)]. -1 means no restriction

subs.description: Max number of subscriptions per connection

data.description: Max number of bytes a connection can send

url.description: Url to the iam-broker Azure connection

code.description: Access code to call the function

initialCapacity.description: The initial size in GB of volumes in this set.

storageClassSuffix.description: For self-hosted locations only. The storage class used for volumes in this set will be {performanceClass}-{fileSystemType}-{storageClassSuffix} if it exists, otherwise it will be {performanceClass}-{fileSystemType}

customEncryption.description: Configure customer-managed encryption keys for volumes in this set on a per-region basis. Region names must follow the format: {cloud-provider}-{region} (e.g., aws-us-east-1).

createFinalSnapshot.description: If true, a volume snapshot will be created immediately before deletion of any volume in this set

retentionDuration.description: The default retention period for volume snapshots. This string should contain a floating point number followed by either d, h, or m. For example, "10d" would retain snapshots for 10 days.

schedule.description: A standard cron schedule expression used to determine when your job should execute.

maxCapacity.description: The maximum size in GB for a volume in this set. A volume cannot grow to be bigger than this.

minFreePercentage.description: The guaranteed free space on the volume as a percentage of the volume's total size. ControlPlane will try to maintain at least that many percent free by scaling up the total size

scalingFactor.description: When scaling is necessary, then new_capacity = current_capacity * storageScalingFactor.

enabled.description: Enable predictive scaling based on historical growth rates. Default: false.

lookbackHours.description: Hours of historical data to analyze. Default: 24. Max: 168 (1 week).

projectionHours.description: Hours into the future to project storage needs. Default: 6.

minDataPoints.description: Minimum data points required for reliable growth rate calculation. Default: 10.

minGrowthRateGBPerHour.description: Minimum growth rate (GB/hour) to trigger predictive expansion. Default: 0.01.

scalingFactor.description: Scaling factor for predictive expansion. If not set, uses the parent autoscaling.scalingFactor. Use a lower value (e.g., 1.2) for gentler proactive scaling.

predictive.description: Predictive scaling configuration. When enabled, proactively expands volumes based on historical growth rate projections.

minMemory.description: Memory allocation specified as a string with units (e.g., 128Mi, 1Gi, 512M). Supports G, M, k, Gi, Mi, Ki suffixes.

maxMemory.description: Memory allocation specified as a string with units (e.g., 128Mi, 1Gi, 512M). Supports G, M, k, Gi, Mi, Ki suffixes.

resources.description: For volume sets using the shared file system, this object specifies the CPU and memory resources allotted to each mount point

mountOptions.description: A list of mount options to use when mounting volumes in this set.

name.description: The name of the location in which this volume was provisioned

storageDeviceId.description: The id of the volume as provided by the underlying storage implementation. If this is blank, an actual storage device has not yet been created.

oldStorageDeviceIds.description: The most recently used storageDeviceId. This is meant for use by Control Plane only

index.description: This number is used to order volumes within the volume set. It is used by Control Plane to link volumes with the workload replicas that use them.

currentSize.description: The current capacity of the volume in GB

currentBytesUsed.description: The total bytes used in the volume.

currentBytesFree.description: The total free bytes available in the volume. Persisted from the latest filesystem stats so the value survives while the volume is unmounted.

driver.description: The name of the CSI driver used to provision and manage this volume

diskType.description: The disk type used for this volume by the underlying cloud provider, for example gp3 on AWS or pd-balanced on GCP. Omitted when the storage backend is not one Control Plane recognizes.

name.description: A human-readable name for this snapshot.

id.description: The id of the snapshot as provided by the underlying storage implementation.

created.description: The date and time that the snapshot was created in the Control Plane API

expires.description: The date and time on which this snapshot will be automatically deleted.

size.description: The size of the snapshot in GB.

node.description: The node hosting this volume, recorded for storage backends whose devices live on a specific node

clusterId.description: The id of the cluster assigned to the gvc in this location.

type.description: Type of workload: standard (always running), cron (scheduled jobs), stateful (persistent state), serverless (rapid autoscaling), or vm (KubeVirt-backed virtual machine).

identityLink.description: The identityLink is used as the access scope for 3rd party cloud resources. A single identity can provide access to multiple cloud providers.

image.description: The full image and tag path for a public or private docker registry. Private container images must have valid credentials configured in 'pullSecretLinks' on the GVC (Global Virtual Cloud). Required for all workload types except 'vm', which boots from spec.vm.bootDisk.source instead.

workingDir.description: The working directory for the container process

port.description: Port where Prometheus metrics are exposed

path.description: HTTP path where Prometheus metrics are exposed

dropMetrics.description: Drop metrics that match given patterns

metrics.description: Prometheus metrics configuration for the container

port.description: The port in the container which receives external traffic or traffic from other workloads. Only one container is allowed to specify a port.

protocol.description: Protocol used by the port (http, http2, grpc, or tcp)

ports.description: The ports in the container which can receive internal and external traffic.  For serverless workloads only the first port will be used.

memory.description: reserved memory of the workload when capacityAI is disabled. maximum memory when CapacityAI is enabled.

volumes.description: Mount Object Store (S3, GCS, AzureBlob) buckets as file system

items.description: The list of ipv4/ipv6 addresses or cidr blocks that are allowed to access this workload. No external access is allowed by default. Specify '0.0.0.0/0' to allow access to the public internet.
The list of ipv4/ipv6 addresses or cidr blocks that are NOT allowed to access this workload. Addresses in the allow list will only be allowed if they do not exist in this list.
DNS hostname with optional wildcard prefix (e.g., *.example.com, example.com)

outboundAllowHostname.description: The list of public hostnames that this workload is allowed to reach. No outbound access is allowed by default. A wildcard '*' is allowed on the prefix of the hostname only, ex: '*.amazonaws.com'. Use 'outboundAllowCIDR' to allow access to all external websites (not recommended). The ports 80, 443 & 445 are allowed by default. This can be modified using the outboundAllowPort setting.

protocol.description: Protocol to allow (http, https, or tcp)

outboundAllowPort.description: Allow outbound access to specific ports and protocols. When not specified, communication to address ranges in outboundAllowCIDR is allowed on all ports and communication to names in outboundAllowHostname is allowed on ports 80/443.

outboundAllowCIDR.description: The list of ipv4/ipv6 addresses or cidr blocks that this workload is allowed reach. No outbound access is allowed by default. Specify '0.0.0.0/0' to allow outbound access to the public internet (not recommended).

outboundBlockedCIDR.description: The list of ipv4/ipv6 addresses or cidr blocks that this workload is NOT allowed reach. Addresses in the allow list will only be allowed if they do not exist in this list.

allowedValues.description:
A list of regular expressions to match for allowed header values. 
Headers that do not match ANY of these values will be filtered and will not reach the workload.

blockedValues.description:
A list of regular expressions to match for blocked header values.
Headers that match ANY of these values will be filtered and will not reach the workload.

items.description: If provided, in order to be an accepted request that is forwarded to the workload, the request must include headers which match the allowedValues regex or must not include headers which match the blockedValues regex.

inboundHeaderFilter.description: A list of header filters for HTTP workloads.

external.description: The external firewall is used to control access to and from the public internet.

inboundAllowType.description: Used to control the internal firewall configuration and mutual tls. 'none': no access is allowed between this workload and other workloads on Control Plane. 'same-gvc': workloads running on the same Global Virtual Cloud are allowed to access this workload internally. 'same-org': workloads running on the same Control Plane Organization are allowed to access this workload internally. 'workload-list': specific workloads provided in the 'inboundAllowWorkload' array are allowed to access this workload internally.

inboundAllowWorkload.description: A list of specific workloads which are allowed to access this workload internally.

internal.description: The internal firewall is used to control access between workloads.

firewallConfig.description: Optional control of inbound and outbound access to the workload for external (public) and internal (service to service) traffic. Access is restricted by default.

target.description: Control Plane will scale the number of replicas for this deployment up/downin order to be as close as possible to the target metric across all replicas of a deployment.

metricPercentile.description: For metrics represented as a distribution (e.g. latency) a percentile within the distribution must be chosen as the target.

maxScale.description: The maximum allowed number of replicas.

minScale.description: The minimum allowed number of replicas.   Control Plane can scale the workload down to 0 when there is no traffic and   scale up immediately to fulfill new requests.

scaleToZeroDelay.description: The amount of time with no requests received before a workload is scaled to 0.

maxConcurrency.description: A hard maximum for the number of concurrent requests allowed to a replica.   If no replicas are available to fulfill the request then it will be queued until a replica with capacity is available   and delivered as soon as one is available again. Capacity can be available from requests completing   or when a new replica is available from scale out. A value of 0 allows all requests.

maxSurgeReplicas.description: Maximum number or percentage of replicas that can be created above the desired count during a rollout

scalingPolicy.description: Determines whether replicas are scaled in order (OrderedReady) or in parallel (Parallel)

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description:
The amount of time in seconds a workload has to gracefully terminate before forcefully terminating it.
This includes the time it takes for the preStop hook to run.

rolloutOptions.description: Configuration for how workload updates are rolled out

runAsUser.description: The user id assigned to all container processes

ipSet.description: IP set to use for dedicated IPs

headers.description: Custom header names for geo location data

replicaDirect.description:
When enabled, individual replicas of the workload can be reached directly using the subdomain prefix replica-<index>.
For example, replica-0.my-workload.my-gvc.cpln.local or replica-0.my-workload-<gvc-alias>.cpln.app
Can only be used with stateful workloads.

retryOn.description: List of conditions that trigger request retries (e.g., 5xx, gateway-error, connect-failure, unavailable)

image.description: Full image reference of a containerDisk (e.g., quay.io/containerdisks/ubuntu:22.04 or /org/<org>/image/<name>:<tag>)

oci.description: Boot from an OCI containerDisk image. Default when no boot source is set; otherwise overrides containers[0].image.

checksum.description: Disk image checksum, formatted as "sha256:<hex>" or "sha512:<hex>"

http.description: Boot disk image fetched over HTTP/HTTPS. Requires persist.volumeSet.

source.description: Exactly one source must be specified.

volumeSet.description: VolumeSet URI used to provision one PVC per replica for the boot disk. Format: cpln://volumeset/<name>.

persist.description: Per-replica boot PVC populated via CDI. Required for any non-OCI source.

bootDisk.description: Boot disk configuration. When source is omitted, containers[0].image is used as an OCI containerDisk.

sockets.description: CPU sockets visible to the guest. Cores are derived from containers[0].cpu.

threads.description: CPU threads per core visible to the guest.

secureBoot.description: Enable UEFI Secure Boot. Not yet supported: pending persistent EFI NVRAM, without which the guest is unbootable after a reboot.

uuid.description: Fixed SMBIOS UUID for the VM. KubeVirt generates one when omitted.

serial.description: SMBIOS system serial number reported to the guest.

guestOS.description: Guest operating system family. Drives per-OS cloud-init payload (file paths, init system, env/hosts injection, SSH CA bootstrap).

networks.description: Pod-network interfaces for the VM. v1 supports a single network; multi-network arrives with per-interface port routing.

userData.description: Inline cloud-init user-data. Not encrypted at rest in the data-service — use userDataSecret for sensitive payloads.

userDataBase64.description: Inline cloud-init user-data, base64-encoded. Same caveats as userData.

userDataSecret.description: Secret containing cloud-init user-data (key: userdata or user-data).

sshPublicKeySecrets.description: SSH public keys injected via cloud-init. Each Secret may carry one or more keys.

runStrategy.description: KubeVirt RunStrategy. Use Halted to keep the pool defined but powered off.

vm.description: VM-only configuration. Required when type=vm; rejected otherwise.

canonicalEndpoint.description: Canonical endpoint URL for the workload

endpoint.description: Primary endpoint URL for the workload

internalName.description: Internal DNS name for the workload

replicaInternalNames.description: Internal DNS names for individual replicas

active.description: Whether the health check is currently active

success.description: Whether the most recent health check succeeded

code.description: HTTP status code from the most recent health check

message.description: Status message from the most recent health check

failures.description: Number of consecutive failed health checks

successes.description: Number of consecutive successful health checks

lastChecked.description: Timestamp of the most recent health check

resolvedForVersion.description: Workload version for which images were resolved

resolvedAt.description: Timestamp when images were last resolved

errorMessages.description: Error messages from image resolution failures

nextRetryAt.description: Timestamp when image resolution will be retried

mediaType.description: Media type of the image manifest

digest.description: Digest SHA of the image manifest

manifests.description: List of image manifests for multi-architecture images

origin.description: Origin location of the load balancer

url.description: URL of the load balancer endpoint
